title: Koszul powers detect supported objects on an affine scheme
statement: Let X=Spec(A) be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let f_1, ..., f_r be elements of A, and let U=X minus V(f_1, ..., f_r). For each tuple e=(e_1, ..., e_r) of positive integers, let K_e be the bounded Koszul complex on f_1^{e_1}, ..., f_r^{e_r}, regarded as a perfect object of D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex]. If E is in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) and E restricted to U is zero, then E=0 whenever Hom(K_e[n],E)=0 for every tuple e and every integer n.

source.place: Tag 09IR, proof using Lemma 36.9.6 and Lemma 36.3.5

proof.text: Fix an integer e\ge1 and the diagonal tuple (e,...,e); the hypothesis gives Hom(K_{(e,...,e)}[m],E)=0 for every integer m. Since U=X minus V(f_1, ..., f_r)=D(f_1)\cup\cdots\cup D(f_r), the represent-cohomology statement [lem-sc-affine-perfect-open-represent-cohomology] supplies perfect objects I_e with distinguished triangles I_e\to O_X\to K_e\to I_e[1], compatible maps u_e:I_e\to O_X, and the isomorphism colim_e Hom(I_e,F)\to H^0(U,F|_U) for every F in D_QCoh(O_X); its K_e is the Koszul complex on f_1^e, ..., f_r^e, which is K_{(e,...,e)} up to a shift of indexing, harmless because the hypothesis holds for every shift. Fix n and apply Hom(-,E[n]) to the triangle: the long exact sequence Hom(K_e,E[n])\to Hom(O_X,E[n])\to Hom(I_e,E[n])\to Hom(K_e,E[n+1]) has vanishing outer terms, so u_e^*:H^n(X,E)=Hom(O_X,E[n])\to Hom(I_e,E[n]) is an isomorphism for every e, compatibly with the transition maps since the u_e are compatible.

Pass to the colimit over e: H^n(X,E)\to colim_e Hom(I_e,E[n]) is an isomorphism (colimit of a system of isomorphisms out of a constant system). Composing with the isomorphism colim_e Hom(I_e,E[n])\to H^0(U,E[n]|_U)=H^n(U,E|_U) of [lem-sc-affine-perfect-open-represent-cohomology], applied to F=E[n] in D_QCoh(O_X), shows H^n(X,E)\cong H^n(U,E|_U)=0, because E restricted to U is zero. Hence H^n(X,E)=0 for every integer n.

By the affine quasi-coherent derived equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], E is isomorphic to the associated complex of R\Gamma(X,E) in D(A), whose cohomology modules are the groups H^n(X,E)=0. So R\Gamma(X,E)=0 in D(A) and therefore E=0 in D_QCoh(O_X).
